[← Back to the deep dive: Document Retrieval](../document-retrieval.qmd)

For end-to-end practice, also use [RAG, memory, and context boundaries](rag-memory-boundaries.qmd). The questions below isolate retrieval and ranking.

## Check your understanding

### 1. Measure candidate recall

A corpus contains 20 documents relevant to a query. The first-stage retriever returns 100 candidates, 8 of which are relevant. Calculate $\mathrm{Recall}@100$. What does this value measure, and what does it not tell you about candidate ordering?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

$$
\mathrm{Recall}@100=\frac{8}{20}=0.4.
$$

The retriever found 40% of the relevant documents in the corpus among its 100 candidates. This measures first-stage coverage; it does not tell us whether relevant documents are placed near the top of the list.

</details>

### 2. The reranker's limit

The first-stage retriever sends no relevant document to the reranking stage. Can a highly capable cross-encoder still place a relevant document in the top 5?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. A reranker reorders the candidates it receives; it cannot retrieve a document that is absent from its input list. Ranking quality is therefore bounded by candidate-generation coverage.

</details>

### 3. Interpret MRR@5

For one query, the first relevant document appears at rank 2 in the reranked list. What is $\mathrm{RR}@5$ for this query? Why should it not be confused with Recall@100?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

$$
\mathrm{RR}@5=\frac{1}{2}=0.5.
$$

Reciprocal rank measures the position of the first relevant result. Recall@100 measures the proportion of all relevant documents retrieved among the 100 candidates. They evaluate different stages and properties.

</details>

### 4. Retrieval succeeds, handoff fails

A relevant passage is retrieved and ranked correctly, but it is dropped while building the prompt because the context budget is exhausted. At which stage did the pipeline fail?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

Retrieval and ranking succeeded; context handoff failed. The model cannot use a passage that was not included in the context it actually received. Retrieval quality alone therefore does not guarantee a source-grounded answer.

</details>
